question.worked_solution:
Recall that if $X=[{X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{k}]^{T}$ is a multivariate normal random vector with mean vector $\mu $ and covariance matrix $Σ,$ then the random variable $Y,$ defined as

$$
Y={c}^{T}X={\sum }_{i=1}^{k}{c}_{i}{X}_{i}
$$

is a normally distributed random variable, where $c$ is any $k\times 1$ column vector, and  

$$
\begin{aligned}E[Y] & ={c}^{T}\mu , \\ Var[Y] & ={c}^{T}Σc.\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, since we wish to know the distribution of $Y=2{X}_{1}+{X}_{2}+2{X}_{3},$ we have 

$$
c=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, for the mean of $Y,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[Y] & ={c}^{T}\mu  \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =-2+0+2 \\  & =0,\end{aligned}
$$

and for the variance of $Y,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[Y] & ={c}^{T}Σc \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 & -1 & 1 \\ -1 & 4 & 2 \\ 1 & 2 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}7 \\ 6 \\ 10\end{aligned}] \\  & =14+6+20 \\  & =40.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
Y∼N(0,40).
$$

Now, we need to compute $P(-6<Y\le 12).$ First, transform $Y$ into a standard normal random variable $Z$ by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-6<Y\le 12) & =P(\frac{-6-0}{\sqrt{40}}<Z\le \frac{12-0}{\sqrt{40}}) \\  & =P(-0.95<Z\le 1.90)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we express the required probability in terms of $Φ(z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-0.95<Z\le 1.90) & =P(Z\le 1.90)-P(Z\le -0.95) \\  & =Φ(1.90)-Φ(-0.95).\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, we know that

$$
\begin{aligned}Φ(0.95) & =0.8289 \\ Φ(1.90) & =0.9713\end{aligned}
$$

By the symmetry of the normal distribution, we have

$$
Φ(-0.95)=1-Φ(0.95)=1-0.8289=0.1711.
$$

As a result,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-0.95<Z\le 1.90)=0.9713-0.1711=0.8002.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
P(-6<Y\le 12)=0.8002.
$$
